en.cta.title: Come throw something on the fire.

en.footer.tagline: Source fully open, architecture written down, and when something breaks you can chase it all the way to the bottom.
en.hero.subtitle: A C++17 and Vulkan core. You write gameplay, tools, render pipelines and models in Python 3.12.
en.home.capabilities.ai.body: Install an InxPackage from a file, folder, Git URL or the official registry. The default MCP package gives agents schema-driven, permission-gated access to the same scene commands and undo path as the editor, without welding agent tooling into the engine core.
en.home.capabilities.ai.title: InxPackage plugins and MCP
en.home.capabilities.animation.body: 2D clips and sprite playback, embedded or separate FBX takes, skeletal animation, skinned meshes, state-machine graphs, Timeline. 0.3.7 maps matching FBX joints exactly, handles importer pivot helpers and rejects incompatible rigs instead of guessing.
en.home.capabilities.animation.title: 2D and 3D animation
en.home.capabilities.asset.body: GUID identity, dependency indexing, imported Library artifacts, live previews, transactional documents. When you export a Player, authoring data and runtime content are two separate things.
en.home.capabilities.asset.title: Assets and project pipeline
en.home.capabilities.data.body: batch_read(cubes, "position") hands you an (N, 3) numpy array in one call. The C++ side keeps that data as a struct of arrays and the GIL stays released for the trip. Writing back works the same way. This is what makes world state visible to a model at all.
en.home.capabilities.data.title: Batch data bridge
en.home.capabilities.editor.body: Hierarchy, Inspector, Scene/Game, Project, Console, UI, animation, Timeline and the graph editors all share one selection, command, shortcut, document, save and undo stack. Useful side effect: an agent drives the editor down exactly the path you do.
en.home.capabilities.editor.title: 12 panels, one command system
en.home.capabilities.intro: 0.3.7 adds a real plugin distribution and lifecycle system, moves MCP into a default package, and fixes skeletal animation imported from separate FBX files. The engine still moves fast, and we still change an interface when it turns out to be wrong.
en.home.capabilities.physics.body: Jolt. Rigid bodies, colliders, scene queries, collision callbacks, layer filtering, transforms kept in sync with the scene. Its job system runs on the engine's own thread pool rather than spawning threads of its own.
en.home.capabilities.physics.title: Jolt physics
en.home.capabilities.render.body: Forward, Forward+ and Deferred paths, PBR, per-camera shadows, MSAA. You describe the pipeline in Python and C++ compiles it into a RenderGraph and schedules it. Effects are reusable assets, and the GLSL is structured rather than one long string.
en.home.capabilities.render.title: Vulkan render core
en.home.capabilities.script.body: Component lifecycle, serialized inspector fields, coroutines, prefabs, hot reload. Close enough to Unity that you will not have to relearn much. Put @njit on a hot function and Numba takes it; where Numba is unavailable it falls back to pure Python instead of blowing up.
en.home.capabilities.script.title: Python gameplay layer
en.home.capabilities.title: The parts you can already work with.
en.home.capabilities.vfx.body: GPU Particle Graph: an emitter plus Init, Update and Rendering stages. The typed graph compiles to runtime IR ahead of time, outputs sprites or meshes, and previews in the editor with parameters you can drag while it runs.
en.home.capabilities.vfx.title: Particle Graph on the GPU
en.home.demo.intro: Not an offline render and not a concept image. Those blocks are ordinary GameObjects going through the ordinary Scene and Hierarchy, with no dedicated batching path. The tilt-shift, fog and colour on top are a RenderStack written in Python.
en.home.demo.panel.item1: 65,536 standard GameObjects sharing one mesh and one material. You can still select them in the Hierarchy and edit them. They are no different from a cube you dropped in by hand.
en.home.demo.panel.item2: Tilt-shift focus, distance fog, height fog, colour controls and MSAA all come from one custom RenderStack. Change it in the editor and you see the result immediately.
en.home.demo.panel.item3: The raw 1920 × 1032 capture from the 0.3.4 showcase. Nothing retouched.
en.home.demo.title: A voxel continent of 65,536 objects, built in the editor and rendered in the editor.
en.home.hero.badge: INFERNUX 0.3.7 · A GAME ENGINE REWRITTEN FOR AI
en.home.hero.description: The Doom generation of engines finished its job a long time ago. Unity and Unreal got the tools into everyone's hands, and now they are fumbling at what this era actually asks for, because whether a model or an agent can really use an engine comes down to its lowest-level data layout, threading model and tool boundaries. None of that can be bolted on afterwards. Infernux starts writing at that layer: agents and the engine collaborating down in the plumbing, not through a chat panel stapled to the side.
en.home.hero.kicker: MIT · open source · Windows x64, downloadable right now
en.home.hero.platform: Windows 10/11 x64 · Infernux 0.3.7 · Android, Web and Linux are next in line
en.home.hero.title: The forge is lit. Come feed the fire.
en.home.manifesto: AI-native is not a chat panel. It means world state you can pull out as a tensor in one call, training that runs inside the editor, and agent-built tools that carry a schema, permissions and tests. None of that can be retrofitted. It has to grow up from the core.
en.home.status.card1.body: 0.3.7 ships InxPackage installation from files, folders, Git and the official registry; MCP is now a removable default package, and separate FBX animation retargeting no longer guesses joints from geometry.
en.home.status.card1.title: Plugins in their own system, animation on the right bones
en.home.status.card2.body: Android and Web game packages plus Torch workflows first. Then Linux and windowless execution, authoritative schemas, replayable batch worlds, the tensor data plane, and Engine Tools that carry permissions and tests.
en.home.status.card2.title: Cross-platform builds, and contracts a model can use
en.home.status.intro: On Windows x64 the whole loop works: create a project, write Python, render, package, ship it. Next that same loop has to run on Android, Web and Linux, with Torch wired into the engine's data plane along the way.
en.home.status.title: 0.3.7 can extend the engine without welding features into its core.
en.home.system.card1.body: Scenes, assets, rendering, physics, UI, animation and packaging stay working. If an AI feature does not make shipping a game better, it does not get merged, however good the demo looks.
en.home.system.card1.title: 1 · It has to be an engine you can ship a game with
en.home.system.card2.body: Gameplay, editor extensions, render pipelines, asset workflows, training scripts: all Python. C++ and the GPU only own performance and deployment. The language you drive the engine with is the language you drive the model with.
en.home.system.card2.title: 2 · Python is not the scripting layer
en.home.system.card3.body: UI, Python, MCP and agents all read the same schema and the same permission set. What a model can call is declared up front, so when it goes wrong you can trace it, undo it, and take the capability back. Without that, do not hand it an engine.
en.home.system.card3.title: 3 · AI comes in the front door
en.home.system.intro: These three regularly make us turn down things that look cool. They are written here so you can hold us to them.
en.home.system.title: Three rules we do not break.
en.home.thesis.card1.body: Pulling rendering, assets and gameplay out of one game and turning them into something you could reuse and license: id Tech settled that in 1993. It was the right problem then. Nobody needs to prove it again.
en.home.thesis.card1.title: The Doom generation already handed in its work
en.home.thesis.card2.body: They did the universal-tooling part well. But Python stays a second-class citizen over there, world state comes out one getattr at a time, and whatever an agent is allowed to touch rests on a script behaving itself. A plugin cannot fix any of that.
en.home.thesis.card2.title: Unity and Unreal are patching AI on from outside
en.home.thesis.card3.body: State sits in C++ as structs of arrays, and one call hands it to Python as a numpy array with the GIL released. An agent drives the same command system you do, and every capability it holds can be audited and taken back. This is the code we write every day.
en.home.thesis.card3.title: Start at the data plane and cut the path through
en.home.thesis.intro: You do not get there by hanging a plugin off a mature engine. How the data is laid out, who is allowed to release the GIL, where the tool boundary sits: all of it has to be decided again, from the core outward.
en.home.thesis.title: Agents and the engine, wired together at the bottom.
en.pageTitle.index: 熔炉 · Infernux — A game engine for the AI era
en.roadmap.hero.description: From a working engine on Windows to cross-platform shipping, models running through the data plane, and agents that can build tools safely. No dates here, only what each step has to do before it counts as done.
en.roadmap.hero.title: Infernux roadmap
en.roadmap.lanes.card1.item1: One project exporting an Android APK/AAB and a Web package you can deploy as it is.
en.roadmap.lanes.card1.item2: A Linux Player, plus windowless and offscreen runs for CI, servers and large-scale simulation.
en.roadmap.lanes.card1.item3: Platform capabilities declared up front, and missing ones failing loudly. No silent downgrades; quiet fallback is a debugging nightmare.
en.roadmap.lanes.card1.title: Shipping
en.roadmap.lanes.card2.item1: Standard PyTorch right in the editor: develop, train, evaluate and export without switching environments.
en.roadmap.lanes.card2.item2: A Player that carries only the inference runtime its platform needs. No CUDA Toolkit, no entire training stack riding along.
en.roadmap.lanes.card2.item3: Every hop between Torch, DLPack and GPU buffers measured, and every copy written down in the docs.
en.roadmap.lanes.card2.title: Model data
en.roadmap.lanes.card3.item1: Versioned reflection plus Command/Query schemas, so UI, Python and MCP read one definition instead of each reimplementing it.
en.roadmap.lanes.card3.item2: World snapshot and delta, deterministic replay contracts, and batched create, step and reset.
en.roadmap.lanes.card3.title: Semantic world
en.roadmap.lanes.card4.item1: An Engine Tool ships with its schema, permissions, tests, provenance, resource limits and lifecycle attached.
en.roadmap.lanes.card4.item2: Plugins and models get a real distribution format, and their own tests run in a sandbox before anything enters your project.
en.roadmap.lanes.card4.item3: Anything an agent builds clears the same bar as human-written code before it goes near someone else's project.
en.roadmap.lanes.card4.title: Tools and ecosystem
en.roadmap.lanes.intro: They share their plumbing. Platform contracts decide where a Player can run. Schemas decide who is allowed to change the world. Replay serves debugging and training equally well. Tool governance covers plugins and agents with the same machinery.
en.roadmap.lanes.title: Four tracks, and they all have to end up in one engine.
en.roadmap.priorities.card1.body: Get a first APK onto real hardware with lifecycle, input, assets, audio, rendering, logs and a minimal portable scripting subset all working in one pass.
en.roadmap.priorities.card1.title: Android Player vertical slice
en.roadmap.priorities.card2.body: Map out the native module, Python, rendering, storage and packaging boundaries in the browser first, then talk about compatibility and performance. This step will probably kill a few assumptions.
en.roadmap.priorities.card2.title: Web portability gate
en.roadmap.priorities.card3.body: Native PyTorch stays in the editor. Which inference backend goes on Android and Web gets decided by measuring model coverage, latency, memory, package size and fallback behaviour, not by picking a favourite.
en.roadmap.priorities.card3.title: Torch entry and the inference backend
en.roadmap.priorities.intro: These have to close real shipping loops. Writing the architecture document does not count, and neither does getting one isolated demo to run.
en.roadmap.priorities.title: The next three.
en.roadmap.release.current.item1: InxPackage plugins install from files, folders, Git and the official registry; MCP now ships as the removable default plugin.
en.roadmap.release.current.item2: Separate FBX animation files map by exact joint identity, accept importer pivot helpers and reject incompatible rigs explicitly.
en.roadmap.release.current.title: Plugin foundations and reliable skeletal animation
en.roadmap.release.long.item1: 0.5.0 formalises Engine Tools and draws a hard line between trusted and untrusted execution. 0.5.1 ships the distribution format for plugins and models, with their own tests run in a sandbox before anything lands in your project.
en.roadmap.release.long.item2: 0.5.2 has to string cross-platform Players, models, schemas, replay, batch worlds and tool governance into one path somebody can walk end to end, live.
en.roadmap.release.long.title: Tools an agent can build, on an engine that holds together
en.roadmap.release.mid.item1: 0.4.1 brings Linux and windowless execution. 0.4.2 sets up the authoritative schemas. 0.4.3 does snapshot, delta and deterministic replay. 0.4.4 opens batch worlds and the tensor data plane.
en.roadmap.release.mid.item2: Every one of these produces a versioned contract and acceptance evidence somebody else can measure. A private path that only survives inside a demo does not count.
en.roadmap.release.mid.title: Headless, semantics, replay, batch data
en.roadmap.release.next.item1: 0.3.7 has to install a first APK on real hardware. 0.3.8 hardens Android inference and packaging. 0.4.0 requires one project to ship on Android and Web at the same time.
en.roadmap.release.next.item2: Torch runs through all three: train and export with native PyTorch in the editor, then swap in whatever inference runtime the target platform can actually carry. Nobody should install a CUDA Toolkit to play a game.
en.roadmap.release.next.title: Android, Web, Torch

zh.footer.tagline: 源码全开，架构写在明处，出了问题你能自己一路查到底。
zh.hero.subtitle: C++17 + Vulkan 的内核。玩法、工具、渲染管线、模型，都用 Python 3.12 写。
zh.home.capabilities.ai.body: InxPackage 可以从文件、目录、Git 地址或官方注册表安装。默认 MCP 包让 Agent 通过 schema 与权限门禁调用和编辑器相同的场景命令与撤销路径，不再把 Agent 工具焊进引擎核心。
zh.home.capabilities.ai.title: InxPackage 插件与 MCP
zh.home.capabilities.animation.body: 2D Clip 与序列帧、FBX 内嵌或独立动画、骨骼动画、蒙皮网格、状态机图、Timeline。0.3.7 精确映射同名 FBX 关节，处理导入器 pivot 辅助节点，并明确拒绝不兼容骨架。
zh.home.capabilities.animation.title: 2D / 3D 动画
zh.home.capabilities.asset.body: GUID 身份、依赖索引、Library 导入产物、实时预览、事务化文档。导出 Player 的时候，创作源数据和运行时内容是分开的两套东西。
zh.home.capabilities.asset.title: 资产与项目管线
zh.home.capabilities.data.body: batch_read(cubes, "position") 一次调用，拿回一个 (N, 3) 的 numpy 数组。数据在 C++ 侧按 SoA 排着，整趟过程 GIL 是放开的。写回同理。模型能不能看见世界状态，卡的就是这一层。
zh.home.capabilities.data.title: 批量数据桥
zh.home.capabilities.editor.body: Hierarchy、Inspector、Scene/Game、Project、Console、UI、动画、Timeline、节点编辑器，共用同一套选择、命令、快捷键、文档、保存和撤销。顺带一个好处：Agent 操作编辑器走的是和你完全相同的那条路。
zh.home.capabilities.editor.title: 12 个面板，一套命令系统
zh.home.capabilities.intro: 0.3.7 加入真正的插件分发与生命周期系统，把 MCP 移进默认插件，并修复从独立 FBX 文件导入的骨骼动画。引擎还在快速改，接口如果确实设计错了，我们照改。
zh.home.capabilities.physics.body: Jolt。刚体、碰撞体、场景查询、碰撞回调、层过滤，变换和场景保持同步。它的作业系统接在引擎自己的线程池上，不会另开一堆线程。
zh.home.capabilities.physics.title: Jolt 物理
zh.home.capabilities.render.body: Forward、Forward+、Deferred 三条路径，PBR，逐相机阴影，MSAA。管线本身用 Python 描述，C++ 把它编译成 RenderGraph 再调度。Effect 是可复用资产，GLSL 是结构化的，不是一坨字符串。
zh.home.capabilities.render.title: Vulkan 渲染内核
zh.home.capabilities.script.body: 组件生命周期、Inspector 序列化字段、协程、Prefab、热重载。写法离 Unity 足够近，基本不用重学。热点函数上加一行 @njit 就交给 Numba；环境跑不了 Numba 时它退回纯 Python，而不是直接炸掉。
zh.home.capabilities.script.title: Python 玩法层
zh.home.capabilities.title: 现在就能拿来干活的部分。
zh.home.capabilities.vfx.body: GPU Particle Graph：一个发射器加 Init / Update / Rendering 三段。类型化的图提前编译成运行时 IR，Sprite 和 Mesh 都能出，编辑器里能预览，参数能一边跑一边拖。
zh.home.capabilities.vfx.title: 跑在 GPU 上的 Particle Graph
zh.home.demo.intro: 不是离线渲染，也不是概念图。这些方块是普通 GameObject，走的是普通的 Scene 和 Hierarchy，没有专门的批渲染通道。上面那层移轴、雾和色彩，是一条用 Python 写出来的 RenderStack。
zh.home.demo.panel.item1: 65,536 个标准 GameObject 共享一套网格和材质。它们在 Hierarchy 里照样能选中、能改，和你手动放进去的那个方块没有任何区别。
zh.home.demo.panel.item2: 移轴对焦、距离雾、高度雾、色彩控制、MSAA，全部来自同一条自定义 RenderStack。在编辑器里改完，当场就能看到结果。
zh.home.demo.panel.item3: 0.3.4 技术展示的原始截图，1920 × 1032，没做后期。
zh.home.demo.title: 65,536 个物体的体素大陆，在编辑器里搭的，也在编辑器里渲的。
zh.home.hero.badge: INFERNUX 0.3.7 · 为 AI 重写的游戏引擎
zh.home.hero.description: Doom 那一代引擎早就完成了历史使命。Unity 和 UE 把工具送到了所有人手上，可面对这个时代的 AI 需求，它们手忙脚乱——因为模型和 Agent 到底能不能用上一台引擎，取决于它最底层的数据排布、线程模型和工具边界，这些东西后期补不上。熔炉从这一层开始写：让 Agent 和引擎在底层就能协作，而不是在旁边挂一个聊天框。
zh.home.hero.kicker: MIT · 开源 · Windows x64 现在就能下
zh.home.hero.platform: Windows 10/11 x64 · Infernux 0.3.7 · 下一批是 Android、Web、Linux
zh.home.hero.title: 熔炉初燃，欢迎来添把火
zh.home.manifesto: AI 原生不是加一个聊天框。它意味着世界状态能一次读成张量，训练就发生在编辑器里，Agent 造出来的工具自带 schema、权限和测试。这些东西没法后期补上，只能从内核往上长。
zh.home.status.card1.body: 0.3.7 支持从文件、目录、Git 和官方注册表安装 InxPackage；MCP 成为可卸载的默认插件，独立 FBX 动画也不再按几何形状猜测关节。
zh.home.status.card1.title: 插件归插件系统，动画回到正确骨骼
zh.home.status.card2.body: 先做 Android 和 Web 的游戏包体加 Torch 工作流。然后是 Linux 与无窗口运行、权威 schema、可回放的批量世界、张量数据面，以及带权限和测试的 Engine Tool。
zh.home.status.card2.title: 跨平台包体，和模型用得上的契约
zh.home.status.intro: 在 Windows x64 上，建项目、写 Python、渲染、打包、发出去，这条链路是通的。接下来同一条链路要跑到 Android、Web 和 Linux 上，同时把 Torch 接进引擎的数据面。
zh.home.status.title: 0.3.7 可以扩展引擎，而不用再把功能焊进核心。
zh.home.system.card1.body: 场景、资产、渲染、物理、UI、动画、打包，这些必须一直是能用的。一个 AI 功能如果不能让做游戏这件事变好，它就不进主干——哪怕 demo 拍出来很好看。
zh.home.system.card1.title: 一 · 它得是台能做完游戏的引擎
zh.home.system.card2.body: 玩法、编辑器扩展、渲染管线、资产流程、训练脚本，全是 Python。C++ 和 GPU 只管性能和部署。你调引擎用的那门语言，和你调模型用的是同一门。
zh.home.system.card2.title: 二 · Python 不是脚本层
zh.home.system.card3.body: UI、Python、MCP、Agent 读的是同一份 schema、同一套权限。模型能调什么是提前声明的，所以出了事能查、能撤、能把权限收回来。做不到这几点，就别把引擎交给它。
zh.home.system.card3.title: 三 · AI 走前门
zh.home.system.intro: 这三条经常让我们拒掉一些看起来很酷的东西。写在这里，你也可以拿它们来质问我们。
zh.home.system.title: 三条我们不打算破的规矩。
zh.home.thesis.card1.body: 把渲染、资源和玩法从一款游戏里剥出来，做成能复用、能授权的东西——1993 年的 id Tech 已经把这件事办完了。那是当时该解决的问题，没人需要再证明一遍。
zh.home.thesis.card1.title: Doom 那一代早就交卷了
zh.home.thesis.card2.body: 工具的通用化它们做得很好。但 Python 在那边始终是二等公民，世界状态得一个个 getattr 才读得出来，Agent 能碰什么全靠脚本自觉。这些都不是加个插件能修的。
zh.home.thesis.card2.era: 手忙脚乱 · 就是现在
zh.home.thesis.card2.title: Unity 和 UE 正在外面给 AI 打补丁
zh.home.thesis.card3.body: 状态在 C++ 里按 SoA 排好，一次调用交给 Python 就是一块 numpy 数组，全程放开 GIL。Agent 走的是和你完全相同的那套命令系统，它拿到的每项能力都能审计、能收回。这就是我们每天在写的代码。
zh.home.thesis.card3.title: 从数据面开始，把路打通
zh.home.thesis.intro: 这件事没法靠在一台成熟引擎旁边挂个插件来做。数据怎么排、谁有权放开 GIL、工具边界画在哪，全都得从内核开始重新决定一遍。
zh.home.thesis.title: 让 Agent 和引擎，在最底层就能协作。

zh.roadmap.hero.description: 从 Windows 上一台能用的引擎，走到跨平台发布、模型贯穿数据面、Agent 能安全造工具。这里不写日期，只写每一格要做到什么才算过。
zh.roadmap.hero.title: 熔炉路线图
zh.roadmap.lanes.card1.item1: 同一个项目导出 Android APK/AAB，也导出能直接部署的 Web 包体。
zh.roadmap.lanes.card1.item2: Linux Player，以及给 CI、服务器和大规模仿真用的无窗口、离屏运行。
zh.roadmap.lanes.card1.item3: 平台能力提前声明，缺什么直接报错。绝不悄悄降级——静默 fallback 是调试地狱。
zh.roadmap.lanes.card1.title: 发布
zh.roadmap.lanes.card2.item1: 编辑器里就是标准 PyTorch，开发、训练、评估、导出都不用换环境。
zh.roadmap.lanes.card2.item2: Player 只带目标平台用得上的推理运行时，不塞 CUDA Toolkit，也不背整个训练栈。
zh.roadmap.lanes.card2.item3: Torch、DLPack、GPU buffer 之间每一跳都测过，每一次拷贝都写进文档。
zh.roadmap.lanes.card2.title: 模型数据
zh.roadmap.lanes.card3.item1: 版本化反射加 Command/Query schema，UI、Python、MCP 读同一份定义，不再各写一遍。
zh.roadmap.lanes.card3.item2: 世界 snapshot 与 delta、确定性回放契约，以及批量的 create、step、reset。
zh.roadmap.lanes.card3.title: 语义世界
zh.roadmap.lanes.card4.item1: Engine Tool 出厂就带着 schema、权限、测试、来源、资源上限和生命周期。
zh.roadmap.lanes.card4.item2: 插件和模型有正式的分发格式，进你的项目之前先在沙箱里跑完它自带的测试。
zh.roadmap.lanes.card4.item3: Agent 造出来的东西想进别人的项目，要过和人写的代码一样的关。
zh.roadmap.lanes.card4.title: 工具与生态
zh.roadmap.lanes.intro: 四条线共用同一批地基：平台契约决定 Player 能跑在哪，schema 决定谁能改世界，回放同时服务调试和训练，工具治理用同一套机制管住插件和 Agent。
zh.roadmap.lanes.title: 四条线，最后得拧成一台引擎。
zh.roadmap.priorities.card1.body: 第一个 APK 装进真机，生命周期、输入、资产、音频、渲染、日志和最小可移植脚本子集，一次跑通。
zh.roadmap.priorities.card1.title: Android Player 垂直切片
zh.roadmap.priorities.card2.body: 先把浏览器里的原生模块、Python、渲染、存储和打包边界摸清楚，再谈兼容性和性能。这一步大概率会推翻几个现在的假设。
zh.roadmap.priorities.card2.title: Web 可移植性关口
zh.roadmap.priorities.card3.body: 编辑器保留原生 PyTorch。Android 和 Web 上用哪个推理后端，靠模型覆盖率、延迟、内存、包体和降级行为量出来，不靠偏好。
zh.roadmap.priorities.card3.title: Torch 入口与推理后端
zh.roadmap.priorities.intro: 这几件事必须闭合真实的发布链路。写完架构文档不算过，跑通一个孤立 demo 也不算。
zh.roadmap.priorities.title: 接下来三关。
zh.roadmap.release.current.item1: InxPackage 可以从文件、目录、Git 和官方注册表安装；MCP 现在作为可卸载的默认插件交付。
zh.roadmap.release.current.item2: 独立 FBX 动画按精确关节名称映射，允许导入器 pivot 辅助节点，并明确拒绝不兼容骨架。
zh.roadmap.release.current.title: 插件基础设施与可靠骨骼动画
zh.roadmap.release.long.item1: 0.5.0 把 Engine Tool 正式化，在可信和不可信执行之间划一条死线。0.5.1 交付插件和模型的分发格式，装进项目之前先在沙箱里跑完它自带的测试。
zh.roadmap.release.long.item2: 0.5.2 要把跨平台 Player、模型、schema、回放、批量世界和工具治理串成一条能当场从头走到尾的路径。
zh.roadmap.release.long.title: Agent 造得出的工具，和一台合得上的引擎
zh.roadmap.release.mid.item1: 0.4.1 上 Linux 和无窗口运行。0.4.2 立起权威 schema。0.4.3 做 snapshot、delta 和确定性回放。0.4.4 打开批量世界与张量数据面。
zh.roadmap.release.mid.item2: 每一格都要交出版本化契约，和别人能复测的验收证据。只在演示里跑得通的私路不算数。
zh.roadmap.release.mid.title: 无窗口、语义、回放、批量数据
zh.roadmap.release.next.item1: 0.3.7 要在真机上装出第一个 APK。0.3.8 打磨 Android 的推理和打包。0.4.0 要求同一个项目能同时发 Android 和 Web。
zh.roadmap.release.next.item2: Torch 贯穿这三关：编辑器里用原生 PyTorch 训练和导出，Player 里换成那个平台真扛得动的推理运行时。玩家不该为了跑一个游戏去装 CUDA Toolkit。
zh.roadmap.release.next.title: Android、Web、Torch
